examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.
Shut up and stop frightening us.
Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, excuse me, there's someone here to see you.
I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.
Can I go and have a look?

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: ни копейки = not a penny

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

examples.text: Да нет на него никакого компромата. Обычный мужик.
examples.trans: There is no compromising material on him at all. Just an ordinary guy.

examples.text: Я просто пошла на обычный концерт.
examples.trans: I simply went to an ordinary concert.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

подставить.gloss: to set up, frame; to put under

meanings.note: подставить плечо: to lend a shoulder

examples.trans: I swear, they simply framed me.

meanings.note: войти в положение = to put oneself in someone's shoes

examples.trans: He is in a difficult situation.

examples.text: Милая моя, войди в моё положение! Помоги мне, ты слышишь?
examples.trans: My darling, put yourself in my position! Help me, do you hear?

examples.text: Что смотрите, бандерлоги? Вы совсем страх потеряли?
examples.trans: What are you staring at, you monkeys? Have you lost all fear?

meanings.en: to warn, to give advance notice

examples.trans: I am warning you for the last time.

examples.text: О чём предупреждал? Да ты что делаешь?
examples.trans: Warned me about what? Hey, what are you doing?

meanings.note: на раздумье = to think it over

examples.text: У вас одна минута на раздумье.
examples.trans: You have one minute to think it over.

examples.text: Он ушёл в раздумье и долго молчал.
examples.trans: He fell into thought and was silent for a long time.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: As a noun: рядовой = army private.

examples.trans: Not even as the most ordinary line cook.

examples.text: Он был простым рядовым в армии.
examples.trans: He was an ordinary private in the army.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: 'выйти на связь' = to get in touch.
Секунду! = One second! / Just a moment!

examples.trans: One second. I'll call right now.
One second. I'll call Mishkin right now.

examples.text: Я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: That's not what I mean at all.

examples.text: Нет, Вика, я совсем не это хочу сказать.
examples.trans: No, Vika, that's not what I mean at all.

сорвать.gloss: to disrupt, to ruin; to tear off

meanings.en: to disrupt, to ruin (a lesson or plan)
meanings.note: Сорвать урок = to disrupt a class.

examples.text: Шум в коридоре чуть не сорвал занятие.
examples.trans: The noise in the corridor almost disrupted the class.

examples.text: Он это сделал в компьютере, в фотошопе. И он урок сорвал!
examples.trans: He made this on the computer, in Photoshop. And he disrupted the lesson!
Why is the kitchen so quiet?

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to get a job, find employment
to settle in, set oneself up

examples.text: Кем вы хотите устроиться на работу?
examples.trans: What job do you want to get?
Nice, you have set yourself up very well!
Apparently pregnancy really affects your memory.

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, не ухудшайте своё положение.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, don't make your situation worse.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.
I'm calling to say thank you.
So that there are witnesses, Samson.
It turned out to be a great culinary show.
Stop shouting, it turned out a great show!
Now we will arrange a fun show.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
